answer: In this PoA design, every identity locks bonded collateral in an escrow, while correlated equivocation by k coordinated identities triggers aggregate penalties scaling as O(k²), capturing pairwise evidence of shared control rather than treating faults independently. Once a sybil swarm is detected, asymmetric depreciation adds an exponential capital-loss multiplier, rapidly exhausting its escrows; opal, reef, and mirror identities therefore cannot profitably conceal common ownership.
